text:
alex: Quick summary from today's cross-region bench of redwood-30B-q4f16 bring-up for Dedicated pools. Ran short + long seqs on h100/eu-west-1 and a100/us-west-2. Posting highlights and proposed reserve/burst plan.

mira: awesome — can you paste the raw numbers?

alex: sure. tl;dr: h100 ~2.8x throughput vs a100 for 512 tokens, gap narrows at 2048. p99 latency on h100 stays <240ms for concurrency<=6 (512 seq). a100 p99 ~420ms at same load. For 2048 seq, p99 h100 ~1.2s at conc=4, a100 ~1.7s.

samir: what concurrency per GPU are we targeting for Dedicated?

alex: target concurrency per GPU: conservative = 4@2048, aggressive = 8@512. That maps to roughly 6 steady-state requests/GPU for mixed traffic (60/40 short/long).

kai: does that include batching + KV cache warmup cost?

alex: yes — numbers include continuous-batching with 40ms batching window and prefix KV cache enabled. Warmup penalty: first 2nd-level request after cold start adds ~150ms on h100 (KV populate). Recommend warmup-runner to prepopulate cache on node boot.

perf-bot: perf alert — p99 > 1s in eu-west-1 h100 pool during ramp at 1839991260 (observed 1.05s), sample workload: seq=2048 conc=6.

bernard: thanks, perf-bot. So what's the recommended reserved count for EU?

alex: proposal: reserve 10 H100 in eu-west-1. Rationale: target 240 QPS equivalent for short-heavy traffic (512), reserve gives headroom for 30% sustained burst and autoscale can add up to +50% (we can set burst to 5 extra nodes). Expected utilization: ~65% at typical day load.

mira: 10 sounds a bit high. cost hit?

alex: estimated committed monthly cost delta vs 8 nodes: +18%. But it keeps p99 under SLO during regional maintenance/evac. If we start with 8 reserved and set autoscale cap=12 that's acceptable too.

samir: for US region (a100) what's the reserve?

alex: reserve 6 A100 in us-west-2, burst cap to 10. We balance because a100 per-GPU throughput lower; we rely on routing policies to send more short-favoring traffic to EU when latency budget allows.

kai: kernel choices? which attention kernel did you run with?

alex: two kernels: Triton fused-attn (default) and fallback cuDNN matmul path. Triton wins on short seqs; cuDNN slightly better memory stack on long seqs in mixed-batch scenarios. For h100 we pinned Triton + kernel=fast_attn; for a100 we used kernel=matmul_opt.

samir: any quality regressions from q4 quant?

alex: small regression on a handful of eval prompts: ~0.9% accuracy drop relative to q8f16 baseline on our redwood-eval set. We tracked via eval-runner and flagged to R&D. For prod policy: enable q4 for latency-sensitive routes but fallback to q8 for high-sensitivity enterprise routes (config flag per route).

mira: autoscale policy snippet?

alex: pasted policy we tested:

```
{"policy":"cpu+token_rate","scale_up_threshold":0.75,"scale_down_threshold":0.35,"min_reserve":8,"max_burst":12,"evaluation_window_ms":60000}
```

kai: small nit: use token_rate instead of cpu for LLM workloads, cpu isn't correlated to latency once batching kicks in.

alex: updated suggestion: change policy to token_rate + p99 latency check.

bernard: warmup plan for new nodes?

alex: warmup-runner process: on node boot, schedule 30s synthetic runs across common prefixes + prefetch model KV for top-50 tokens. Script: `./warmup.sh --model redwood-30B-q4f16 --clients 4 --prefetch 50` — reduces first-request penalty to ~30-50ms after boot.

devops-bot: note — reserved change requires quota ticket. Raising ticket now (TICKET-4392).

mira: regression monitoring — can we tie eval set to rollout? gate q4 rollout behind quality gating at 0.5% drop threshold.

samir: agreed. also add canary rule: route 10% traffic to q4 pools for 24h, compare rouge/accuracy, then widen.

alex: final ask: can infra provision 8-10 h100 in eu-west-1 as start, set autoscale min=8 max=12, warmup enabled, and route policy to prefer eu for short seq?

kai: will do. raising infra PR shortly.

alex: thanks — will follow up with a brief doc + heatmap export (link will be posted here). :thumbsup:

bernard: marked — we'll review after the canary window.
